title: Weight-ferry lane and KV shadow preheat for dedicated throughput SLAs
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Design and implement a lightweight 'weight-ferry' lane plus a KV shadow preheat controller to reduce cold-start latency for Dedicated capacity fleets while preserving throughput guarantees. The feature complements existing warm pools by enabling incremental background weight transfers (rate-limited ferrying) and speculative KV fingerprinting that primes shard-local caches without committing full weight residency, allowing faster on-traffic handoffs and lower cost of standby capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start 95th-percentile latency for customer 'fastpath' tenants decreases by >=35% in our dedicated fleet benchmark
Throughput nodal SLA (tokens/sec per GPU) remains within 3% of baseline under steady state when ferry lanes are active
KV shadow preheat does not increase memory pressure beyond configured thresholds and can be toggled per-tenant
Expose telemetry in Console: per-tenant ferry-rate, shadow-hit-rate, and cold-start reduction metric panels
Automated canary rollout via console with abort on >5% error increase or >10% latency regression
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype weight-ferry process that streams small weight fragments from cold storage to GPU-resident staging buffer; implement rate limiter and per-tenant priority queue (ENG-176004-PR1)

Phase 2: KV shadow preheat controller — use cheap fingerprint probes to populate shard-local KV bloom filters and lightweight caches without full KV materialization; add eviction hooks tied to ferry progress
Phase 3: Admission controller integration — coordinate ferry + existing warm-pool admission to prevent double-counting capacity and avoid throughput cliffs
Phase 4: Observability — add ferry metrics (bytes/sec, fragments in-flight), shadow-hit-rate, cold-start delta and surface on Console dashboards (grafana.redwood.internal/dashboard/ferry)
Phase 5: Canary rollout on dedicated pool subset; collect perf & cost signals; iterate on heuristics and per-tenant hysteresis
Phase 6: Docs + SDK flags — document config knobs (ferry_rate, shadow_enabled, tenant_hysteresis_window) and add runtime feature flag for Private deployments
risks: If ferry rate is mis-tuned it can saturate network/SSD burst limits and temporarily degrade steady-state throughput
Speculative KV fingerprinting might create false sense of cache readiness causing increased tail latency if miss rates under real traffic are higher
Complexity in admission logic could introduce oscillation between warm-pool allocations and ferry activity without proper hysteresis
Rolling back after a bad rollout requires careful draining of partially-ferried weights to avoid inconsistent model binaries
notes: Related tickets: ENG-30512 (initialization handoff), ENG-21009 (anticipatory residency controller)
Storage interaction pattern defined to use staged SSTable reads and read-ahead bundling to reduce IOPS pressure
We decided to avoid eager full-weight snapshotting for low-priority tenants to keep cost predictable (feedback from customer X)

2025-11-05 Ravi Kapoor: Implemented ferry prototype (branch ferry/proto). Small end-to-end run against local dedicated-fleet shows stable throughput but elevated SSD read bursts. Filed follow-up to batch reads into 16MB windows.

2025-11-06 Design review (Ava Mitchell): UX asks for per-tenant visibility and an opt-out toggle in Console. Added 'shadow_enabled' config flag and per-tenant hystersis settings to implementation plan.
2025-11-08 PM review (Diego Morales): Requested clear rollback procedure and that canary abort conditions be conservative. Added abort thresholds to acceptance criteria and plan.
2025-11-10 QA update (Priya Nair): End-to-end tests added. Observed 7% throughput variance under synthetic burst tests; tuning ferry_rate to 40MB/s per-node reduced variance below 3%.
